analysis: Aspirin causes platelet dysfunction by inhibiting the cyclooxygenase enzyme, leading to reduced thromboxane A2 production and impaired platelet aggregation. This increases the risk of bleeding, especially when combined with heparin, which also prevents clot formation through a different mechanism (enhancement of antithrombin III). The combined effect of these drugs significantly elevates the risk of bleeding, making the use of aspirin in a patient already on heparin generally contraindicated due to this compounded bleeding risk.
